Original · Unique Research · 2025-12-02

Historical edition: The rankings, market observations, research-methodology claims and forecasts below are those published by Unique Research in December 2025 about October 2025. They are preserved as historical reporting, not independently verified current results. The title’s 3.8 billion users is the source headline, not a claim of 3.8 billion deduplicated individual people. Download and active-user totals across products must not be read as a deduplicated population.

If you looked only at app-store rankings, the AI world in October would feel familiar: ChatGPT and Gemini were still at the top, while the apps domestic users opened most often remained Doubao, DeepSeek, and Tencent Yuanbao. On the surface, everything stayed in its usual steady state, with gateway-level "super apps" continuing to command the greatest share of attention.

But when Unique Research's data for the October 2025 Global AI App Top 100 is laid out in full, a much more nuanced picture emerges. The Top 100 recorded about 570 million downloads in total that month, yet the products truly lifting the growth curve were those embedded in specific use cases such as search, learning, and personal assistance: Perplexity was accelerating in search, education apps such as Gauth were scaling rapidly, and a new generation of AI assistants was beginning to evolve from "chat tools" into "everyday workspaces."

Based on Unique Research's monitoring data for the October Global AI App Top 100 by monthly downloads, this report reviews a month of "surface stability and structural fine-tuning" from several perspectives—overall scale, geographic composition, category shifts, and representative apps—to identify the quietly rising trends that product and startup teams should really watch.

I. Overall Landscape: 570 Million Downloads, Highly Concentrated but Growing Moderately

ChatGPT recorded about 93.64 million downloads in October, down about 6% month over month.

Google Gemini recorded about 73.64 million, down nearly 18% month over month.

Perplexity ranked third with about 30.40 million downloads, up nearly 45% month over month.

Cici AI recorded about 14.91 million and continued its steady rise, up about 5% month over month.

Gauth, a representative education app, reached 26.69 million downloads in a single month, an increase of nearly 300% month over month.

Taken together, ChatGPT and Gemini accounted for close to 30% of all Top 100 downloads, showing that "general conversational gateways" still possess overwhelming user-acquisition power. Their month-over-month trajectories, however, show that they have moved beyond the explosive early phase of acquiring new users and entered a stage more like "infrastructure"—stable and enormous in scale, but no longer doubling every month.

Overall, among the 98 apps with month-over-month data, about 57% increased their downloads and 43% declined. The median month-over-month increase was about 4.2%, while the average was around 10%. In other words, the AI App market continued to expand in October, but at a gentler pace driven more closely by real demand.

II. Geographic Structure: The Overseas Market Is Largest, While Global-Bound Apps Grow Fastest

By geography, the 100 apps on the list included 55 overseas products, 22 domestic products, and 23 global-bound products created by Chinese teams. Their approximate download volumes were:

Overseas apps: about 333 million, accounting for about 58%, with average month-over-month growth of about 7.6%.

Domestic apps: about 146 million, accounting for about 25%, with average month-over-month growth of about 11.9%.

Global-bound apps: about 95 million, accounting for about 16.6%, with average month-over-month growth of about 15.7%.

In one sentence: scale is overseas, while growth is in global-bound and domestic apps.

Narrowing the view to the top 20 reveals a more balanced combination: 8 overseas apps, 7 domestic apps, and 5 global-bound apps. In other words, the products with a real chance of entering the "top-tier club" are no longer limited to a few European and American giants. Chinese teams serving the domestic and global markets are appearing near the top of the rankings with increasing frequency.

On the domestic side, the mix includes general-purpose assistants such as DeepSeek and Tencent Yuanbao, as well as established products deeply rooted in local use cases, including Meitu, BeautyCam, Zuoyebang, and Xiaoyuan Kousuan. Together they form a two-pillar structure of "basic tools + education."

The global-bound segment leans more clearly toward "vertical capabilities + global distribution." Gauth, Cici, Seekee, and various AI video and image tools, for example, project Chinese teams' algorithmic and engineering advantages to users worldwide through productization and ASO/paid-acquisition capabilities.

III. Category Reshuffling: Chatbots Hold the Gateway While Search and Education Accelerate

Grouping the Top 100 by product type brings the details into sharper focus.

The categories with the highest downloads in October were:

Chatbots: 15 apps with about 251 million downloads in total, accounting for 43.9% of the Top 100; average month-over-month growth was almost 0, while the median was about 4.4%.

Image editing: 15 apps with about 66.18 million downloads in total, accounting for 11.5%; average month-over-month growth was about 5.6%, while the median was nearly flat.

Education: 18 apps with about 58.68 million downloads in total, accounting for 10.2%; average month-over-month growth was about 33%, while the median was about 7%.

Intelligent search: 4 apps with about 54.20 million downloads in total, accounting for 9.5%; average month-over-month growth was about 23%.

Personal assistants: 7 apps with about 49.75 million downloads in total, accounting for 8.7%; average month-over-month growth was about 27%.

Although deeper-use-case categories such as education, search, and personal assistants still trail general chat in scale, they are clearly showing more vigorous growth.

By contrast, several typical categories that "went viral early" have begun to cool collectively:

Image generation: 3 apps with about 7.44 million downloads in total; average month-over-month growth was about -21.6%, while the median was about -33%. SeaArt, Jimeng, and others all pulled back.

Some video-editing and filter products: overall downloads remained substantial, but average month-over-month growth was about -5.7%. Domestic apps including Jimeng AI, Kuaiying, and several AI portrait apps all posted double-digit declines.

Certain utility categories, such as text-to-speech and motion capture, remain relatively small overall and also showed negative month-over-month growth, indicating that they "have not yet found a sufficiently large, must-have use case."

Put simply, users are shifting from "playing with AI effects" to "using AI to get things done." The rapid growth of education, search, and personal assistants is the data-driven expression of that preference.

IV. Several Representative Directions: User Choices Behind the Data

Looking at several growth curves within the rankings makes the picture more three-dimensional.

The first curve comes from search and Q&A.

Perplexity recorded about 30.40 million downloads in October, up nearly 47% month over month, vaulting into third place. Domestically, Quark - Your AI Search and Baidu with Full-Power DeepSeek Integration maintained steady growth, each at roughly 7 million downloads and up about 12% and 15%, respectively. In the global-bound segment, Seekee also exceeded 10 million monthly downloads, up about 19%.

What these products share is that they transform AI, in the task of "finding information," from a simple question-answering tool into a comprehensive tool that "searches and evaluates on your behalf." The data clearly indicate that users are willing to pay for this added layer of capability.

The second curve is education.

This category appeared to "accelerate collectively" in October. The 18 education apps generated about 58.68 million downloads in total, with average month-over-month growth reaching 33%. Gauth alone recorded 26.69 million downloads, up nearly 300%; domestic apps such as Xiaoyuan Search, Daxue Soutijiang, and Kuaidui AI also grew by anywhere from 40%–160% month over month.

More interestingly, established overseas learning tools have begun to diverge:

Quizlet, which introduced AI early, declined nearly 42% month over month in October, and Photomath also fell. Meanwhile, a new generation of "AI-native" learning, speaking-practice, and children's education apps continued to climb. The education sector appears to be undergoing a "generational" product renewal.

The third curve is personal assistants.

Domestic apps Tencent Yuanbao and DeepSeek maintained steady growth at around the 20 million level, each up about 4% to 5% month over month. Overseas, Meta AI and Grok were among the few new assistants in this ranking that truly "scaled up": Meta AI recorded about 10.77 million downloads, up more than 150%, while Grok approached 10 million downloads, up more than 50%.

Personal-assistant apps share the goal of evolving from "a chat box" into "a workspace that can get things done for you": beyond chat, they connect to search, documents, social platforms, content consumption, and even desktop systems. The Top 100 data suggest that users are gradually forming a habit of keeping an "always-on AI assistant."

The fourth curve is the divergence among image and video tools.

Image editing provides a typical example: leading products Meitu and BeautyCam recorded about 20.22 million and 4.46 million downloads, respectively, both growing by around 47% month over month; overseas product Photo Lab grew by more than 100%. Within the same category, however, some apps focused more narrowly on "AI portraits" or a single style, such as Xinghui - AI Portrait Camera, declined by more than 70% month over month.

Video showed a similar pattern. Products combining AI capabilities with general editing functions, such as Invideo AI and Beat.ly, continued to grow within a range of +12% to +52% month over month, while purer "technology-showcase" video generators generally pulled back.

Taken together, these curves tell the same story: users are more willing to pay for AI capabilities that integrate reliably into everyday work and life than to linger over momentary novelty.

V. Domestic vs. Global-Bound: The Same AI Capabilities, Different Paths to Market

Returning the focus to Chinese products reveals two interesting contrasts.

On one side is the domestic market.

The domestic Top 22 apps generated about 146 million downloads in October, with average month-over-month growth close to 12%. Beyond "general gateways" such as Doubao, DeepSeek, and Tencent Yuanbao, education and utility apps actually account for a large share:

K12 and parent tools: Zuoyebang, Xiaoyuan Kousuan, Xiaoyuan Search, Daxue Soutijiang, and others embed AI in already-active education App ecosystems through common use cases such as question search, homework checking, and after-school tutoring.

Search and browsing: Quark, Baidu with DeepSeek integration, Starry Browser, and others "wrap AI capabilities in familiar product shells," lowering the learning cost.

Image editing: Meitu products continue to leverage their integrated strengths in "tools + content + community," retaining considerable vitality after their AI upgrades.

On the other side are global-bound apps.

The global-bound Top 23 apps generated about 95 million downloads in October, with average month-over-month growth of about 16%, the fastest among the three major markets.

Representative products include, on the one hand, "AI-native products" explicitly targeting global users, such as Gauth, Cici, and Seekee; on the other, BeautyPlus, Hypic, UpFoto, and various AI video tools that take China's already-mature image and video editing capabilities, upgrade them with AI, and relaunch them into global markets.

The same underlying AI capabilities face entirely different retention dynamics:

Domestic users are more accustomed to integrating AI into frequent, must-have use cases such as learning, tools, and search. Global users, across a wider range of languages and cultures, are exploring which scenarios should be rebuilt with AI. The Top 100 data can be viewed as an interim verdict—which paths are working smoothly, and which may require timely retreat.

02. Research Statement

2.1 Data Notes

The AI product revenue data in this report, article, ranking, or chart are based on real-time tracking of referral traffic from AI product websites to payment gateways such as Stripe. Combined with time-series analysis, this process examines historical visits, fluctuations in monthly active users, and changes in pricing strategies to build a dynamic revenue-estimation model. The model's core parameters are determined through a three-part validation system: monitoring paid-conversion funnels, reverse-calibrating against company disclosures, and comparing industry-benchmark conversion rates. They are also promptly compared with and adjusted against corporate financial reports, financing announcements, and disclosures by authoritative media. Sampling validation shows that the mean absolute error rate between predicted and actual values remains within ±10%, meeting industry research-grade accuracy standards.

The AI product traffic data in this report, article, ranking, or chart are based on the integration of multiple data sources and processing by Unique Research's intelligent algorithms. Monitoring is strictly limited to users' direct access through official apps and websites. Specifically, these data cover only direct user access to AI products through websites and native applications; they exclude traffic generated through browser plugins/extensions, desktop client software, WeChat/Alipay mini-program ecosystems, services embedded in third-party platforms such as Discord, local deployment of open-source models, API calls, and other indirect-access scenarios. The data focus on direct user behavior at AI products' core endpoints, with the aim of objectively reflecting direct usage by mainstream end users.

Given the complexity and dynamic nature of data collection and processing, as well as ongoing changes in the market environment, the data presented may contain some errors and omissions. They should therefore be regarded as references for research and analysis, intended to provide a window into the AI product market rather than as a definitive basis for specific investment strategies or advisory recommendations.

2.2 Definitions

• Geographic Dimensions

Overseas AI products: products founded by entrepreneurs or teams not of Chinese heritage and launched primarily for global markets, including but not limited to their home markets.

Domestic AI products: products founded by Chinese-national entrepreneurs or teams and launched primarily for China's domestic market.

Global-bound AI products: products founded by entrepreneurs or teams of Chinese heritage but primarily targeting overseas markets outside mainland China.

• Functional Dimensions

AI-native applications: applications that have deeply integrated artificial-intelligence technology and algorithms from the outset of product design, and whose core value, business processes, or user experience depends entirely on AI technology. These applications do not merely use AI to optimize or enhance existing features; they make AI a core component, without which the applications would cease to exist or lose their core value.

AI-enabled applications: applications that integrate or embed AI technology into existing business logic and application frameworks to enhance existing functions or provide entirely new ones. These applications may already have mature business models and market positioning, but the introduction of AI can significantly improve efficiency, enhance user experience, or create new value.

AI-ecosystem applications: platform applications that support, connect, or facilitate communication among the developers, application builders, service providers, end users, and other participants who make up the AI ecosystem. These applications are not limited to technology; they also involve markets, communities, resource sharing, and other dimensions, with the aim of promoting the adoption, innovation, and collaboration of AI technology.

2.3 Metric Notes

• WEB Data Metrics

Visits: the total number of all visits to a website during a specific period, such as one month, used to measure the scale of website traffic. Page views during a continuous active period count as one session, while renewed activity after an interval of more than 30 minutes or the beginning of a new day is counted as a new visit, thereby providing a comprehensive and precise measure of website traffic and visitor activity.

Unique Visitors: the number of unique IP addresses visiting the target website during a specific period, such as one month. If someone visits a website on multiple days within one month, that person is counted as only one unique visitor.

Subscription revenue (labeled ARR in the source): all revenue that a website earns by providing subscription services during a given period, such as one year; this excludes advertising revenue, transaction commissions, professional services, and other one-time revenue.

• APP Data Metrics

Downloads: the number of times an App is downloaded during a specific period, such as one month. It is usually measured by the number of downloads of an individual App from app stores such as the App Store and Google Play. Downloads are an important metric for assessing an App's popularity and ability to attract users, and can also reflect the results of App promotion and marketing campaigns.

Active Users: the number of unique users who perform at least one activity during a specific period, such as one month. Active users measure user scale and activity during a given period and are commonly used to evaluate an App's user base and level of engagement.

In-App Purchase Revenue (IAP): revenue generated when users purchase virtual goods, additional services, premium features, and other items within an App. This excludes advertising revenue, direct user payments such as tips, and revenue from third-party Android app stores.

Appendix: Summary of Quarterly Trend Insights

Looking at the October data as a whole produces a straightforward impression: the AI App story is not over; it has simply entered a new stage. Over the past two years, we became accustomed to using downloads to judge whether a product had "taken off." Now, monthly active users, usage frequency, and the contexts in which users spend time are gradually becoming more important metrics. Downloads measure curiosity; monthly activity measures genuine attachment. The structure of this Top 100 essentially makes that point through data.

At the category level, gateway chatbots have secured their position as "infrastructure," and disruptive change is unlikely in the short term. The lines truly rising are narrower ones: AI search is quietly taking over the information gateway; learning apps are reconstructing the everyday routines of "finding answers, tutoring, and exam preparation"; utility and creative products are integrating AI into concrete work steps such as design, editing, and copywriting. Users have not left AI; they have moved from "casually trying it" to "using it for serious work."

Geographically, overseas markets remain the front line for acquiring new users, with new AI applications constantly emerging. The domestic market looks more like a "battlefield for retained attention": many products no longer pursue spectacular new-user numbers every month, instead steadily defending a fixed share of usage time. Global-bound apps, meanwhile, are in a period of frequent experimentation, placing the same technologies and models into different cultures and needs to test which combinations can accumulate a truly stable active-user base. For Chinese teams, these three markets form a complete pathway: refine use cases domestically, test product forms overseas, and then scale what works.

More importantly, the data carry a practical reminder for product builders: over the next one or two years, the opportunity in AI Apps will most likely lie not in "building yet another new gateway," but in "taking the same technology deep into a use case others lack the patience to tackle." Whoever truly understands how users allocate the 24 hours in their day—and makes their product the default choice for several critical actions—will continue to appear in future rankings. Buzz remains important, but a product's fate is ultimately determined by those quiet, repeatedly occurring moments of use.

Historical edition: The rankings, market observations, research-methodology claims and forecasts below are those published by Unique Research in December 2025 about October 2025. They are preserved as historical reporting, not independently verified current results. The title’s 3.8 billion users is the source headline, not a claim of 3.8 billion deduplicated individual people. Download and active-user totals across products must not be read as a deduplicated population.

If you looked only at app-store rankings, the AI world in October would feel familiar: ChatGPT and Gemini were still at the top, while the apps domestic users opened most often remained Doubao, DeepSeek, and Tencent Yuanbao. On the surface, everything stayed in its usual steady state, with gateway-level "super apps" continuing to command the greatest share of attention.

But when Unique Research's data for the October 2025 Global AI App Top 100 is laid out in full, a much more nuanced picture emerges. The Top 100 recorded about 570 million downloads in total that month, yet the products truly lifting the growth curve were those embedded in specific use cases such as search, learning, and personal assistance: Perplexity was accelerating in search, education apps such as Gauth were scaling rapidly, and a new generation of AI assistants was beginning to evolve from "chat tools" into "everyday workspaces."

Based on Unique Research's monitoring data for the October Global AI App Top 100 by monthly downloads, this report reviews a month of "surface stability and structural fine-tuning" from several perspectives—overall scale, geographic composition, category shifts, and representative apps—to identify the quietly rising trends that product and startup teams should really watch.

I. Overall Landscape: 570 Million Downloads, Highly Concentrated but Growing Moderately

ChatGPT recorded about 93.64 million downloads in October, down about 6% month over month.

Google Gemini recorded about 73.64 million, down nearly 18% month over month.

Perplexity ranked third with about 30.40 million downloads, up nearly 45% month over month.

Cici AI recorded about 14.91 million and continued its steady rise, up about 5% month over month.

Gauth, a representative education app, reached 26.69 million downloads in a single month, an increase of nearly 300% month over month.

Taken together, ChatGPT and Gemini accounted for close to 30% of all Top 100 downloads, showing that "general conversational gateways" still possess overwhelming user-acquisition power. Their month-over-month trajectories, however, show that they have moved beyond the explosive early phase of acquiring new users and entered a stage more like "infrastructure"—stable and enormous in scale, but no longer doubling every month.

Overall, among the 98 apps with month-over-month data, about 57% increased their downloads and 43% declined. The median month-over-month increase was about 4.2%, while the average was around 10%. In other words, the AI App market continued to expand in October, but at a gentler pace driven more closely by real demand.

II. Geographic Structure: The Overseas Market Is Largest, While Global-Bound Apps Grow Fastest

By geography, the 100 apps on the list included 55 overseas products, 22 domestic products, and 23 global-bound products created by Chinese teams. Their approximate download volumes were:

Overseas apps: about 333 million, accounting for about 58%, with average month-over-month growth of about 7.6%.

Domestic apps: about 146 million, accounting for about 25%, with average month-over-month growth of about 11.9%.

Global-bound apps: about 95 million, accounting for about 16.6%, with average month-over-month growth of about 15.7%.

In one sentence: scale is overseas, while growth is in global-bound and domestic apps.

Narrowing the view to the top 20 reveals a more balanced combination: 8 overseas apps, 7 domestic apps, and 5 global-bound apps. In other words, the products with a real chance of entering the "top-tier club" are no longer limited to a few European and American giants. Chinese teams serving the domestic and global markets are appearing near the top of the rankings with increasing frequency.

On the domestic side, the mix includes general-purpose assistants such as DeepSeek and Tencent Yuanbao, as well as established products deeply rooted in local use cases, including Meitu, BeautyCam, Zuoyebang, and Xiaoyuan Kousuan. Together they form a two-pillar structure of "basic tools + education."

The global-bound segment leans more clearly toward "vertical capabilities + global distribution." Gauth, Cici, Seekee, and various AI video and image tools, for example, project Chinese teams' algorithmic and engineering advantages to users worldwide through productization and ASO/paid-acquisition capabilities.

III. Category Reshuffling: Chatbots Hold the Gateway While Search and Education Accelerate

Grouping the Top 100 by product type brings the details into sharper focus.

The categories with the highest downloads in October were:

Chatbots: 15 apps with about 251 million downloads in total, accounting for 43.9% of the Top 100; average month-over-month growth was almost 0, while the median was about 4.4%.

Image editing: 15 apps with about 66.18 million downloads in total, accounting for 11.5%; average month-over-month growth was about 5.6%, while the median was nearly flat.

Education: 18 apps with about 58.68 million downloads in total, accounting for 10.2%; average month-over-month growth was about 33%, while the median was about 7%.

Intelligent search: 4 apps with about 54.20 million downloads in total, accounting for 9.5%; average month-over-month growth was about 23%.

Personal assistants: 7 apps with about 49.75 million downloads in total, accounting for 8.7%; average month-over-month growth was about 27%.

Although deeper-use-case categories such as education, search, and personal assistants still trail general chat in scale, they are clearly showing more vigorous growth.

By contrast, several typical categories that "went viral early" have begun to cool collectively:

Image generation: 3 apps with about 7.44 million downloads in total; average month-over-month growth was about -21.6%, while the median was about -33%. SeaArt, Jimeng, and others all pulled back.

Some video-editing and filter products: overall downloads remained substantial, but average month-over-month growth was about -5.7%. Domestic apps including Jimeng AI, Kuaiying, and several AI portrait apps all posted double-digit declines.

Certain utility categories, such as text-to-speech and motion capture, remain relatively small overall and also showed negative month-over-month growth, indicating that they "have not yet found a sufficiently large, must-have use case."

Put simply, users are shifting from "playing with AI effects" to "using AI to get things done." The rapid growth of education, search, and personal assistants is the data-driven expression of that preference.

IV. Several Representative Directions: User Choices Behind the Data

Looking at several growth curves within the rankings makes the picture more three-dimensional.

The first curve comes from search and Q&A.

Perplexity recorded about 30.40 million downloads in October, up nearly 47% month over month, vaulting into third place. Domestically, Quark - Your AI Search and Baidu with Full-Power DeepSeek Integration maintained steady growth, each at roughly 7 million downloads and up about 12% and 15%, respectively. In the global-bound segment, Seekee also exceeded 10 million monthly downloads, up about 19%.

What these products share is that they transform AI, in the task of "finding information," from a simple question-answering tool into a comprehensive tool that "searches and evaluates on your behalf." The data clearly indicate that users are willing to pay for this added layer of capability.

The second curve is education.

This category appeared to "accelerate collectively" in October. The 18 education apps generated about 58.68 million downloads in total, with average month-over-month growth reaching 33%. Gauth alone recorded 26.69 million downloads, up nearly 300%; domestic apps such as Xiaoyuan Search, Daxue Soutijiang, and Kuaidui AI also grew by anywhere from 40%–160% month over month.

More interestingly, established overseas learning tools have begun to diverge:

Quizlet, which introduced AI early, declined nearly 42% month over month in October, and Photomath also fell. Meanwhile, a new generation of "AI-native" learning, speaking-practice, and children's education apps continued to climb. The education sector appears to be undergoing a "generational" product renewal.

The third curve is personal assistants.

Domestic apps Tencent Yuanbao and DeepSeek maintained steady growth at around the 20 million level, each up about 4% to 5% month over month. Overseas, Meta AI and Grok were among the few new assistants in this ranking that truly "scaled up": Meta AI recorded about 10.77 million downloads, up more than 150%, while Grok approached 10 million downloads, up more than 50%.

Personal-assistant apps share the goal of evolving from "a chat box" into "a workspace that can get things done for you": beyond chat, they connect to search, documents, social platforms, content consumption, and even desktop systems. The Top 100 data suggest that users are gradually forming a habit of keeping an "always-on AI assistant."

The fourth curve is the divergence among image and video tools.

Image editing provides a typical example: leading products Meitu and BeautyCam recorded about 20.22 million and 4.46 million downloads, respectively, both growing by around 47% month over month; overseas product Photo Lab grew by more than 100%. Within the same category, however, some apps focused more narrowly on "AI portraits" or a single style, such as Xinghui - AI Portrait Camera, declined by more than 70% month over month.

Video showed a similar pattern. Products combining AI capabilities with general editing functions, such as Invideo AI and Beat.ly, continued to grow within a range of +12% to +52% month over month, while purer "technology-showcase" video generators generally pulled back.

Taken together, these curves tell the same story: users are more willing to pay for AI capabilities that integrate reliably into everyday work and life than to linger over momentary novelty.

V. Domestic vs. Global-Bound: The Same AI Capabilities, Different Paths to Market

Returning the focus to Chinese products reveals two interesting contrasts.

On one side is the domestic market.

The domestic Top 22 apps generated about 146 million downloads in October, with average month-over-month growth close to 12%. Beyond "general gateways" such as Doubao, DeepSeek, and Tencent Yuanbao, education and utility apps actually account for a large share:

K12 and parent tools: Zuoyebang, Xiaoyuan Kousuan, Xiaoyuan Search, Daxue Soutijiang, and others embed AI in already-active education App ecosystems through common use cases such as question search, homework checking, and after-school tutoring.

Search and browsing: Quark, Baidu with DeepSeek integration, Starry Browser, and others "wrap AI capabilities in familiar product shells," lowering the learning cost.

Image editing: Meitu products continue to leverage their integrated strengths in "tools + content + community," retaining considerable vitality after their AI upgrades.

On the other side are global-bound apps.

The global-bound Top 23 apps generated about 95 million downloads in October, with average month-over-month growth of about 16%, the fastest among the three major markets.

Representative products include, on the one hand, "AI-native products" explicitly targeting global users, such as Gauth, Cici, and Seekee; on the other, BeautyPlus, Hypic, UpFoto, and various AI video tools that take China's already-mature image and video editing capabilities, upgrade them with AI, and relaunch them into global markets.

The same underlying AI capabilities face entirely different retention dynamics:

Domestic users are more accustomed to integrating AI into frequent, must-have use cases such as learning, tools, and search. Global users, across a wider range of languages and cultures, are exploring which scenarios should be rebuilt with AI. The Top 100 data can be viewed as an interim verdict—which paths are working smoothly, and which may require timely retreat.

02. Research Statement

2.1 Data Notes

The AI product revenue data in this report, article, ranking, or chart are based on real-time tracking of referral traffic from AI product websites to payment gateways such as Stripe. Combined with time-series analysis, this process examines historical visits, fluctuations in monthly active users, and changes in pricing strategies to build a dynamic revenue-estimation model. The model's core parameters are determined through a three-part validation system: monitoring paid-conversion funnels, reverse-calibrating against company disclosures, and comparing industry-benchmark conversion rates. They are also promptly compared with and adjusted against corporate financial reports, financing announcements, and disclosures by authoritative media. Sampling validation shows that the mean absolute error rate between predicted and actual values remains within ±10%, meeting industry research-grade accuracy standards.

The AI product traffic data in this report, article, ranking, or chart are based on the integration of multiple data sources and processing by Unique Research's intelligent algorithms. Monitoring is strictly limited to users' direct access through official apps and websites. Specifically, these data cover only direct user access to AI products through websites and native applications; they exclude traffic generated through browser plugins/extensions, desktop client software, WeChat/Alipay mini-program ecosystems, services embedded in third-party platforms such as Discord, local deployment of open-source models, API calls, and other indirect-access scenarios. The data focus on direct user behavior at AI products' core endpoints, with the aim of objectively reflecting direct usage by mainstream end users.

Given the complexity and dynamic nature of data collection and processing, as well as ongoing changes in the market environment, the data presented may contain some errors and omissions. They should therefore be regarded as references for research and analysis, intended to provide a window into the AI product market rather than as a definitive basis for specific investment strategies or advisory recommendations.

2.2 Definitions

• Geographic Dimensions

Overseas AI products: products founded by entrepreneurs or teams not of Chinese heritage and launched primarily for global markets, including but not limited to their home markets.

Domestic AI products: products founded by Chinese-national entrepreneurs or teams and launched primarily for China's domestic market.

Global-bound AI products: products founded by entrepreneurs or teams of Chinese heritage but primarily targeting overseas markets outside mainland China.

• Functional Dimensions

AI-native applications: applications that have deeply integrated artificial-intelligence technology and algorithms from the outset of product design, and whose core value, business processes, or user experience depends entirely on AI technology. These applications do not merely use AI to optimize or enhance existing features; they make AI a core component, without which the applications would cease to exist or lose their core value.

AI-enabled applications: applications that integrate or embed AI technology into existing business logic and application frameworks to enhance existing functions or provide entirely new ones. These applications may already have mature business models and market positioning, but the introduction of AI can significantly improve efficiency, enhance user experience, or create new value.

AI-ecosystem applications: platform applications that support, connect, or facilitate communication among the developers, application builders, service providers, end users, and other participants who make up the AI ecosystem. These applications are not limited to technology; they also involve markets, communities, resource sharing, and other dimensions, with the aim of promoting the adoption, innovation, and collaboration of AI technology.

2.3 Metric Notes

• WEB Data Metrics

Visits: the total number of all visits to a website during a specific period, such as one month, used to measure the scale of website traffic. Page views during a continuous active period count as one session, while renewed activity after an interval of more than 30 minutes or the beginning of a new day is counted as a new visit, thereby providing a comprehensive and precise measure of website traffic and visitor activity.

Unique Visitors: the number of unique IP addresses visiting the target website during a specific period, such as one month. If someone visits a website on multiple days within one month, that person is counted as only one unique visitor.

Subscription revenue (labeled ARR in the source): all revenue that a website earns by providing subscription services during a given period, such as one year; this excludes advertising revenue, transaction commissions, professional services, and other one-time revenue.

• APP Data Metrics

Downloads: the number of times an App is downloaded during a specific period, such as one month. It is usually measured by the number of downloads of an individual App from app stores such as the App Store and Google Play. Downloads are an important metric for assessing an App's popularity and ability to attract users, and can also reflect the results of App promotion and marketing campaigns.

Active Users: the number of unique users who perform at least one activity during a specific period, such as one month. Active users measure user scale and activity during a given period and are commonly used to evaluate an App's user base and level of engagement.

In-App Purchase Revenue (IAP): revenue generated when users purchase virtual goods, additional services, premium features, and other items within an App. This excludes advertising revenue, direct user payments such as tips, and revenue from third-party Android app stores.

Appendix: Summary of Quarterly Trend Insights

Looking at the October data as a whole produces a straightforward impression: the AI App story is not over; it has simply entered a new stage. Over the past two years, we became accustomed to using downloads to judge whether a product had "taken off." Now, monthly active users, usage frequency, and the contexts in which users spend time are gradually becoming more important metrics. Downloads measure curiosity; monthly activity measures genuine attachment. The structure of this Top 100 essentially makes that point through data.

At the category level, gateway chatbots have secured their position as "infrastructure," and disruptive change is unlikely in the short term. The lines truly rising are narrower ones: AI search is quietly taking over the information gateway; learning apps are reconstructing the everyday routines of "finding answers, tutoring, and exam preparation"; utility and creative products are integrating AI into concrete work steps such as design, editing, and copywriting. Users have not left AI; they have moved from "casually trying it" to "using it for serious work."

Geographically, overseas markets remain the front line for acquiring new users, with new AI applications constantly emerging. The domestic market looks more like a "battlefield for retained attention": many products no longer pursue spectacular new-user numbers every month, instead steadily defending a fixed share of usage time. Global-bound apps, meanwhile, are in a period of frequent experimentation, placing the same technologies and models into different cultures and needs to test which combinations can accumulate a truly stable active-user base. For Chinese teams, these three markets form a complete pathway: refine use cases domestically, test product forms overseas, and then scale what works.

More importantly, the data carry a practical reminder for product builders: over the next one or two years, the opportunity in AI Apps will most likely lie not in "building yet another new gateway," but in "taking the same technology deep into a use case others lack the patience to tackle." Whoever truly understands how users allocate the 24 hours in their day—and makes their product the default choice for several critical actions—will continue to appear in future rankings. Buzz remains important, but a product's fate is ultimately determined by those quiet, repeatedly occurring moments of use.
